review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped it for simp attributes and for uses of the small rewrite lemmas. The file has no @[simp] declarations, and the header only removes simp lemmas from other files. All findings are about missing simp lemmas or attributes, based on how the file's own proofs use the lemmas. I did not run Lean. The suggestions are untested, and I did not check whether Mathlib already has simp lemmas for `1 ⊗ₜ c` (for example `includeRight`). Of the many other rewrite lemmas, I flagged only ones with repeated, concrete uses.

findings.excerpt: theorem emb_one : emb (K := K) (L := L) (v := v) (1 : F) = 1 := rfl
findings.problem: `emb` is an irreducible-to-simp plain `def` (`1 ⊗ₜ c`), and its homomorphism laws `emb_mul`, `emb_one` and `emb_zero` carry no simp attribute. Each use therefore passes them by hand: `simp [Matrix.map_apply, c1, c2, h01, h10, emb_zero]` (l.617), `simp only [c1, ..., emb_mul]` (l.641, 648), `simp [act, c1, c2, emb_one]` (l.657), and `rw [← emb_mul, ..., emb_one]` in `isUnit_emb`. Since `emb` is not unfolded by simp, plain `simp` cannot normalise `emb (c*d)`, `emb 1` or `emb 0` unless the user remembers the names.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `emb_mul`, `emb_one` and `emb_zero` with `@[simp]`. The shape is the usual one for a multiplicative hom (`f (a*b) = f a * f b`, `f 1 = 1`, `f 0 = 0`), the left-hand side head `emb` is a stable normal form, and there is no loop risk. Alternatively, define `emb` as a `RingHom` (`Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight`) so that the generic `map_mul`, `map_one` and `map_zero` simp lemmas apply. Then drop the explicit `emb_*` arguments at l.617, 641, 648 and 657.
findings.benefit: The `fin_cases ... <;> simp` proofs about `c1`, `c2`, `act` and `coe_toTensorGL_of_mem` no longer need hand-supplied lemma names. Later proofs about `emb` get normalised automatically.

evidence.excerpt: simp [Matrix.map_apply, c1, c2, h01, h10, emb_zero]

findings.problem: These two lemmas describe the underlying matrix of `sigmaGL g` and `toTensorGL t` as `Matrix.map`. They are not simp lemmas, and every consumer must follow them with `Matrix.map_apply` to reach entries. The same two-lemma pattern is written by hand in four places: `simp only [coe_sigmaGL, Matrix.map_apply]` (l.343), `rw [← map_inv, coe_sigmaGL, Matrix.map_apply]` (l.348), `simp only [coe_toTensorGL, Matrix.map_apply]` (l.1021) and `rw [← map_inv, coe_toTensorGL, Matrix.map_apply]` (l.1025). The `Matrix.map` form is the wrong form for the entrywise goals these proofs actually have (`... i j`). `coe_sGL` (l.507) is stated, but the continuity proof of `sGL` (l.~525) bypasses it with `change Continuous fun q : Q => sm q`.
findings.proposed_change: Add entrywise lemmas such as `coe_sigmaGL_apply : ((sigmaGL K L F σ g : G) : Matrix _ _ E) i j = sigmaTensor K L F σ ((g : Matrix _ _ E) i j)` and `coe_toTensorGL_apply : ((toTensorGL K L F t : G) : Matrix _ _ E) i j = emb ((t : Matrix _ _ F) i j)`, both provable by `rfl`, and mark them `@[simp]`. They are also stable normal forms (the right-hand side has smaller structure). Mark `coe_sGL` `@[simp]` as well, or use it in `continuous_sGL`. Then the four sites reduce to `simp` or a single `rw`.
findings.benefit: This removes the repeated two-step rewrite pattern. It gives `simp` a canonical entrywise form for matrices of twisted or embedded group elements, so later `fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp` proofs about them (for example `toTensorGL_mul_diag`) can see the entries without manual unfolding.

findings.excerpt: theorem D_of_not {p : Q} (hp : p ∉ goodT) : D (K := K) (L := L) (v := v) p = 0 := by
findings.problem: The conditional rewrite lemmas for the chart `uGL`, the density `D`/`Dr`, and `mk''` of `sm` have no simp attribute. The same hand-written `rw` chains are therefore repeated verbatim in two places: `rw [uGL_of_mem h1, mk''_sm, D_of_mem (show p ∈ goodT from h1)]` and `rw [dif_neg h, D_of_not (show p ∉ goodT from h), zero_mul, mul_zero]` (l.753–754), and again in `solution` (l.1299–1300). The membership proofs must be coerced with `show p ∈ goodT from h1`, because `goodT` membership is not syntactically the `IsUnit ... det` hypothesis. The dependent-hypothesis `D_of_mem` and `Dr_of_mem` also each re-derive their statements by `simp [Dr, hp]` instead of sharing a simp-usable unconditional form. `mk''_sm` has a proof argument `h` that does not appear in the right-hand side, so it is an ideal unconditional simp lemma (the `h` becomes an ordinary argument that unifies).
findings.proposed_change: Mark `mk''_sm` `@[simp]`; its proof argument is irrelevant to the right-hand side, so it never blocks matching. Mark the side-condition lemmas `uGL_of_not`, `D_of_not` and `Dr_of_not` `@[simp]` (they are conditional rewrites whose hypothesis simp can discharge). Add `mem_goodT_iff` as simp, so the hypothesis `p ∉ goodT` is rewritten to `¬(IsUnit p.1 ∧ IsUnit p.2)`. State `D_of_mem` and `Dr_of_mem` with hypotheses in the form `IsUnit (tm p).det` or `IsUnit p.1 ∧ IsUnit p.2`. Then the two copies of the block collapse to `simp [uGL_of_mem h1, D_of_mem ...]` or similar. Alternatively keep them as `rw` lemmas but state `D_of_mem` with `(tm p).det` so that `h1` can be passed directly.
findings.benefit: The two near-identical 3-step rewrite blocks (l.753–754 and l.1299–1300) become simp-dischargeable. The `show _ ∈ goodT from ...` casts disappear, and the unit-chart and density lemmas form a coherent, discoverable simp set.
